Information since November points to a strong labor market and solid activity, with robust household spending and a moderation in business fixed investment—consistent with textbook findings that investment is more volatile than consumption. With inflation near 2% and longer-term expectations little changed, the Committee’s emphasis on a symmetric target and gradualism accords with New Keynesian guidance that anchoring expected inflation (e.g., Woodford) is central, and with inflation-forecast targeting ideas (Svensson). Raising the federal funds target to 2.25–2.50% and setting IOER at 2.40%—while maintaining ON RRP operations and balance-sheet runoff caps—mirrors Taylor-rule-style responses to the economic state and reflects the Friedman–Phelps view that there is no exploitable long-run unemployment–inflation trade-off. Monitoring global and financial conditions is also in line with research linking macro factors to term premia and long-term rates (e.g., Ang–Piazzesi; Rudebusch–Wu). Overall tone: constructive but slightly hawkish given continued tightening and softer capex.
